facts.statement: Edentosuchus is a member of the protosuchian crocodyliform group.
facts.quote: Edentosuchus is a genus of protosuchian crocodyliform.

facts.statement: Fossils of Edentosuchus come from the Early Cretaceous Tugulu Group in the Junggar Basin of Xinjiang, China.
facts.quote: It is known from fossils found in rocks of the Early Cretaceous-age Tugulu Group from the Junggar Basin, Xinjiang, China.

facts.statement: The known remains include two partial skulls and several neck vertebrae.
facts.quote: Two partial skulls and several neck vertebrae are known to date.

facts.statement: The type species is Edentosuchus tienshanensis.
facts.quote: The type species is E. tienshanensis.

facts.statement: A joint expedition between the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County and the National Geological Museum of China recovered another partial skull in 2000.
facts.quote: A joint Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County-National Geological Museum of China expedition recovered another partial skull in 2000.

facts.statement: While originally placed in its own family, later research determined Edentosuchus belongs to the family Protosuchidae.
facts.quote: Yang originally assigned it to its own family (Edentosuchidae) within Protosuchia, but later research by Diego Pol and colleagues using the new material found it to be a protosuchid.

facts.statement: Edentosuchus is classified within the parent group Protosuchidae.
The teeth at the tip of the upper jaw were conical.
facts.quote: In the upper jaw, the teeth in the tip of the snout (premaxillae) were conical.

facts.statement: The first two teeth of the upper jaw behind the tip had three cusps.
facts.quote: Following them, the first two teeth of the maxillae had three cusps.

facts.statement: The next two upper jaw teeth had numerous small cusps, while the fifth and last were bulbous, larger than the others, and featured small cusps.
facts.quote: The next two had numerous small cusps, and the fifth and last was bulbous, larger than others, and featured small cusps.

facts.statement: The skull was only a few centimetres long, featuring a short, relatively narrow snout and a wide posterior section.
facts.quote: The skull was only a few centimetres (or inches) long, and had a short, relatively narrow snout and wide posterior section.

facts.statement: Edentosuchus lived between 199.5 and 184.2 million years ago during the Sinemurian to Pliensbachian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Sinemurian to Pliensbachian (199.5 to 184.2 million years ago)

facts.statement: Contemporary fauna included turtles, dsungaripterid pterosaurs, and various dinosaurs such as theropods, sauropods, stegosaurs, psittacosaurids, and ornithopods.
facts.quote: Living alongside it were turtles, dsungaripterid pterosaurs, and theropod, sauropod, stegosaurian, psittacosaurid, and ornithopod dinosaurs.

facts.statement: New fossil material of Edentosuchus tienshanensis from the Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation was described by Tan et al. in 2026.
facts.quote: Tan et al. (2026) describe new fossil material of Edentosuchus tienshanensis from the Lower Cretaceous Lianmuqin Formation (Xinjiang, China), providing new information on the morphology of members of this species.
